title: Naturality and K-flat computation of the tensor augmentation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in a coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes and their unbounded derived category with localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $T(A,B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R B)$ with the signed direct-sum total [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and use the derived tensor and its specified K-flat representative comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. There is a canonical natural transformation on pairs of complexes
$$\rho_{A,B}:QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QB\longrightarrow Q T(A,B).$$
For arbitrary cochain maps $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$ its naturality equation is
$$Q T(a,b)\circ\rho_{A,B}=\rho_{A',B'}\circ(Qa\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Qb).$$
For K-flat complexes $P,Q'$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $\rho_{P,Q'}$ is the inverse of the specified representative isomorphism $QT(P,Q')\cong QP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QQ'$. For any K-flat resolutions $p:P\to A$ and $q:Q'\to B$ with flat terms, its normalization is
$$\rho_{A,B}\circ(Qp\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Qq)=QT(p,q)\circ\rho_{P,Q'}.$$
This construction is independent of the resolution choices. No boundedness or flatness of $A,B,A',B'$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0FPH, label lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility, canonical horizontal tensor arrows and their computation by the two resolution augmentations in the proof.

proof.text:
Write $D(f,g)=Qf\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Qg$ for maps of complexes. For flat-term K-flat $P,N$ let $c_{P,N}:QT(P,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}QP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QN$ be the specified comparison. The descent node supplies this isomorphism and its naturality. Choose resolutions $p:P\to A$, $q:N\to B$ using the resolution node. Since localization inverts their quasi-isomorphisms, $D(p,q)$ is invertible. Define
$$r(p,q)=QT(p,q)\circ c_{P,N}^{-1}\circ D(p,q)^{-1}.$$
It has source $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QB$ and target $QT(A,B)$; the ordinary target is not asserted to invert quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction), and 0FPH (lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility), horizontal resolution arrows.

proof.text:
First compare resolutions related by maps. Let $u:P_0\to P$ and $v:N_0\to N$ be quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes. Naturality of $c$ gives
$$QT(u,v)\circ c_{P_0,N_0}^{-1}=c_{P,N}^{-1}\circ D(u,v).$$
Functoriality gives $QT(pu,qv)=QT(p,q)QT(u,v)$ and $D(pu,qv)=D(p,q)D(u,v)$. Substitution in the definition in step 1 cancels $D(u,v)$ with its inverse, giving $r(pu,qv)=r(p,q)$. This uses only the specified comparison on K-flat pairs; no inverse of an ordinary tensor augmentation is used.

source.place: Tag 06YU, independence of resolution; naturality of the K-flat representative comparison.

proof.text:
For two arbitrary choices $(p_i:P_i\to A,q_i:N_i\to B)$, $i=1,2$, apply strict-diagram replacement to the finite cospan $P_1\to A\leftarrow P_2$, and separately to $N_1\to B\leftarrow N_2$. It gives flat-term K-flat complexes $X_i,U,Y_i,V$, quasi-isomorphisms $e_i:X_i\to P_i$, $r:U\to A$, $f_i:Y_i\to N_i$, $s:V\to B$, and strict arrows $u_i:X_i\to U$, $v_i:Y_i\to V$ with $ru_i=p_ie_i$ and $sv_i=q_if_i$. These arrows are quasi-isomorphisms: on every cohomology object $H^n(u_i)=H^n(r)^{-1}H^n(p_i)H^n(e_i)$, and similarly for $v_i$. Step 2 therefore gives
$$r(p_i,q_i)=r(p_ie_i,q_if_i)=r(ru_i,sv_i)=r(r,s).$$
Thus both choices give the same morphism. Define $\rho_{A,B}$ to be this choice-independent value.

source.place: Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero) via the existing strict-diagram replacement theorem; Tag 06YU resolution independence. The finite-cospan argument is an agent expansion.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$, replace the two walking-arrow diagrams by the strict-diagram theorem. This supplies flat-term K-flat resolutions $p:P\to A$, $p':P'\to A'$, $q:N\to B$, $q':N'\to B'$ and maps $\alpha:P\to P'$, $\beta:N\to N'$ with $ap=p'\alpha$ and $bq=q'\beta$. Neither $\alpha$ nor $\beta$ need be quasi-isomorphisms. Functoriality and comparison naturality give
$$QT(a,b)QT(p,q)=QT(p',q')QT(\alpha,\beta),\qquad QT(\alpha,\beta)c_{P,N}^{-1}=c_{P',N'}^{-1}D(\alpha,\beta),$$
$$D(\alpha,\beta)D(p,q)^{-1}=D(p',q')^{-1}D(a,b).$$
Inserting these three identities into step 1 gives
$$QT(a,b)\rho_{A,B}=QT(p',q')c_{P',N'}^{-1}D(p',q')^{-1}D(a,b)=\rho_{A',B'}D(a,b).$$
Step 3 permits these diagram-adapted choices. This proves naturality on pairs of complexes, without descending $QT$ to pairs of derived objects.

source.place: Tag 0FPH (lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility), resolution augmentation computation; Tag 077J via the strict-diagram replacement theorem. The displayed naturality calculation is an agent expansion.

proof.text:
If $P,N$ already are K-flat with flat terms, take their identity maps as resolutions in step 1. All identity factors disappear, so $\rho_{P,N}=c_{P,N}^{-1}$. For arbitrary resolutions $p:P\to A$, $q:N\to B$, multiply the defining formula on the right by $D(p,q)$ to obtain
$$\rho_{A,B}D(p,q)=QT(p,q)c_{P,N}^{-1}=QT(p,q)\rho_{P,N}.$$
This is the requested normalization for every choice by step 3. Existence of the resolutions and all diagram replacements used above hold for unbounded complexes, so no boundedness or flatness assumption has been imposed on $A,B,A',B'$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unique_ringedTensorAugmentation : ∃! ρ : ringedTensorAugmentationSource R ⟶ ringedTensorAugmentationTarget R, ∀ (P N : CochainComplex (Modules R) ℤ) (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients P) (hN : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients N) (hPf : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (P.X n)) (hNf : ∀ n : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (N.X n)), ρ.app (P, N) = (representativeIso R P N hP hN hPf hNf).inv ∧ ∀ (A B : CochainComplex (Modules R) ℤ) (p : P ⟶ A) (q : N ⟶ B), QuasiIso p → QuasiIso q → (ringedTensorAugmentationSource R).map (Prod.mkHom p q) ≫ ρ.app (A, B) = ρ.app (P, N) ≫ (ringedTensorAugmentationTarget R).map (Prod.mkHom p q)
lean.note: The natural transformation is on pairs of actual complexes; its naturality is structural.
